books.section: Prosperity and a New World Order (1988–2000)

stem: Comparing 1982 and 2009, which pattern does the table best support?

options.text: Unemployment spikes only during Democratic presidencies
options.misconception: 1982 fell under a Republican president and 2009 under a Democrat, so party does not explain the spikes.
The table rises and falls: 9.7 percent in 1982, 4.0 percent in 2000, then 9.6 percent in 2010.

options.text: Severe recessions can push unemployment above 9 percent in very different eras
Unemployment in 2009 was caused by the same stock bubble as in 2000
options.misconception: The 2009 spike came from the housing and banking crisis, not the internet-stock bubble of 2000.

rationales.A: 1982 fell under a Republican president and 2009 under a Democrat. Background: party does not explain the spikes.
rationales.B: The table rises and falls: 9.7 percent in 1982, 4.0 percent in 2000, then 9.6 percent in 2010.
rationales.C: The table shows unemployment above 9 percent in 1982 and again in 2009–2010, in two very different recessions.
rationales.D: Background: the 2009 spike came from the housing and banking crisis, not the internet-stock bubble of 2000.
rationales.general:
1. Put the two spikes side by side: 9.7 percent in 1982, 9.3 percent in 2009.
2. Note how different the eras are — one under Reagan, one under Obama, with different causes.
3. What they share is severity: a deep recession can push joblessness past 9 percent in any decade.
4. Party labels and single causes fail, because the two spikes disagree with them.
Remember: the same number in two eras means the pattern is the recession, not the decade.
